newsitem.title: USA: First Alert sees $9.5 mln Q4 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: First Alert sees $9.5 mln Q4 restructuring charge.

text.p: First Alert Inc said Monday it will take a pre-tax charge in the fourth quarter of about $9.5 million, or $0.23 a share as part of a restructuring.
Before the charge, the company estimated it incurred an operating loss of about $4.5 million to $5.0 million, or about $0.18-$0.20 a share, in the quarter.

The charge includes costs for inventory and manufacturing equipment write-downs and severance costs as the company repositions, reduces or exits product lines that are secondary to its smoke detector and carbon monoxide detector business, the company said.
The company has also reduced staffing levels by 600 full-time equivalents with an estimated annual cost savings of $3 million, First Alert said.
First Alert said it expects revenues in the fourth quarter were about $60 million, down from the $76.4 million reported in the year ago period.
First Alert would not disclose how many employees it had before the staffing cuts.
The company also said results from the restructuring would not immediately reach the bottomline.

"The still inappropriately high levels of inventory we have on hand as we enter our slowest selling periods will delay the effect of these actions being seen in any dramatic bottom-line turnaround," First Alert chief executive officer B. Joseph Messner said in a news release. But he added that the actions should help position the company for improved sustainable profitability in the future.

"First Alert's primary focus is the residential safety marketplace and on the opportunities which exist within its core product categories for smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors," Messner said, adding the company is udnertaking actions to strengthen the lines.

Emphasis is on product design and features in smoke detectors, while the company is also undertaking similar efforts in carbon monoxide detectors, while focusing and building consensus among standards-setting organizations.
First Alert shares rose 1/4 to four Monday. The company said it expects to report fourth quarter results toward the beginning of February.
